messages.author: 3d0cccc7ec805901
messages.subject: rrook with invisible R ("standalone script")
parts:
Hi all,

is it possible to run a rrook application with R's internal server in
an Rscript (or so), i.e. R running invisibly in the background? The
idea is to make it easy to use for people who have no clue about R;
they would just use the interface in a browser.

When I start a rrook application from a script having
"#!/usr/bin/Rscript --vanilla" as the first line, the application is
started but R runs through the rest of the script and terminates, so
that no further user interaction with the rrook application is
possible. So, how could R stay running in the background?

(I am interested in using it in both GNU/Linux and Windows.)

Thanks for any ideas,

Sven

messages.author: 2e6cf6b360029e14
messages.subject: Re: rrook with invisible R ("standalone script")
parts:
Hi Sven-

Adding something at the end of your script like:

while(T) {
Sys.sleep(10000)
}

will keep the server running indefinitely. You'll also need to background the script (e.g., with `nohup` on *nix) or run it under a screen so it doesn't exit when the user logs out. I would still suggest running the script under some sort of process manager (for *nix, something like Bluepill, God, etc.) to ensure it restarts if it were to crash. (you can also do something like run it on Heroku, which takes care of keeping the process running indefinitely -- I posted instructions for how to get Rook running on Heroku a couple weeks ago on this list).

Noah
